title: Your backtest bought at $100. When did it actually know to buy?
author: Electrical_Waltz_888
selftext:
Say your rule is: “Buy if the daily candle closes above $99.”

The candle closes at $100. Your backtest sees the signal and buys at $100. The next session opens at $103.

That $3 difference isn’t just a slippage setting. If your strategy needs the final close to confirm the signal, it needs a separate rule for when it can submit the order. A backtest that gives you the closing price needs to explain how that order could have been placed and filled.

Here’s the question I’d give AI before trusting the equity curve:

>Review this backtest rule: \[paste rule\]. For each trade, separate when the signal becomes knowable, when the order can first be submitted, and what price the test assumes it gets. Flag any fill that relies on information the system wouldn’t have had when it placed the order. If the data can’t establish the fill, say so.

Then rerun it with a fill assumption that matches when the strategy could actually act. How much of the result survives that one change?

Disclosure: I wrote *The Complete Guide to AI Powered Trading* It covers how to use AI to question backtest assumptions and includes 50 reusable prompts.

comments.author: Tradenoss
comments.body: one more case worth adding to that prompt: gaps on the exit side. if the next open is already through your stop, the realistic stop fill is the open, not the stop price. plenty of daily-close tests fix the entry and still fill the exit at the level.
